about: Where the texts still missing from each rite can come from, in the order they should be imported. A source listed here is a lead, not a clearance: check the exact scan, edition and territory before extracting, as docs/source-review.md requires. Run `python3 tools/text_sources.py --audit` to re-check every Internet Archive identifier.

rights.pd: Published before 1931: public domain in the United States. Print after checking the scan matches the edition named.
rights.pd-reprint: A later facsimile or reprint of a pre-1931 text. The text is public domain; transcribe from it but cite the original edition.
rights.ancient: Latin, Greek, Syriac or Ge'ez liturgical text of ancient or medieval origin in a later edition. Print what is traceable to a pre-1931 source; leave out anything newly composed for that edition.
rights.open: Openly licensed data or software (licence named in the note). Check that the licence actually covers the text, not only the code.
rights.check-renewal: United States publication 1931-1963. Public domain only if the copyright was not renewed: search the Copyright Office renewal records before importing.
rights.check-uraa: Foreign publication 1931 or later. May have had its US copyright restored; treat as protected unless the source-country term had expired by 1996.
rights.permission: In copyright. Cite and cue it; reproduce only with written permission from the holder named in the note.
rights.reference: Study or calendar reference only. Not a text to print.
rights.crown-uk: Public domain outside the United Kingdom; Crown rights in the UK (existing project policy for the 1662 Prayer Book).
rights.policy: In copyright, but the holder publishes the text free and its policy allows some reproduction without asking (terms in the note). Check that the terms cover this site before printing; otherwise treat as permission.

gaps.plan: No public-domain English exists for the 1970/2002 Missal. Three steps reach the most text: (1) print the Graduale Romanum Introit and Communion, which the GIRM allows in place of the Missal antiphons, from GregoBase (CC0) using the Ordo cantus Missae assignments; (2) map each oration to its ancient source and print the public-domain Latin with a public-domain English where one exists; (3) offer the Roman Canon (already printed) as the default Eucharistic Prayer. Collects composed after 1965, the new prefaces and Eucharistic Prayers II-IV stay cued unless ICEL (English) or the Libreria Editrice Vaticana (Latin) grants permission.

gaps.plan: Most of the Office is older than its 1971 edition. Hymns: the Latin originals are public domain (Divinum Officium's breviary hymns, noting where the 1971 hymnal restored pre-1632 wording), with English from the English Hymnal and The Hymner. Second readings in the Office of Readings are patristic: print them from the Schaff Ante-Nicene and Nicene Fathers on CCEL once the two-year and one-year cycles are tabulated (the tables are facts). Concluding prayers are the Missal collects, so they follow the Mass plan. Antiphons and responsories are mostly Scripture and can be shown as the verse in Douay-Rheims, labelled as such. Intercessions are modern compositions and stay cued.

gaps.plan: These books are in copyright but free to download, and several churches publish reuse policies. Common Worship is the strongest case: the Church of England allows its online texts to be reproduced on another non-commercial website if unaltered and acknowledged. ACNA allows liturgies in worship bulletins and short quotations (up to 2,500 words or 10%). New Zealand and Canada allow parish copies only. Build cited guides for all of them, print Common Worship under its web terms once someone confirms they cover an app, and ask the other holders.
